parameter_matrix.note: A part wins only if its operating Vin range strictly encompasses the counterpart on both ends.
Higher Vin,abs improves survivability against hot-plug and inductive bus spikes.
Tighter Vout tolerance improves ADC reference and digital rail margin.
Actual usable continuous Iout is also bounded by package θJA thermal derating.
Lower Iq directly extends sleep-mode battery life in always-on IoT/portable rails.
Lower dropout allows regulation deeper into Li-ion / 3.7 V discharge curves.

parameter_matrix.note: Non-ceramic-stable LDOs oscillate with low-ESR MLCCs unless series resistance or tantalum is used.
Higher PSRR attenuates upstream switching-converter ripple on analog/RF rails.
Critical for RF VCOs, low-noise ADCs, and precision sensor excitation.
Lower θJA yields lower junction temperature rise ΔTj = (Vin - Vout) × Iout × θJA.
Keep steady-state Tj at least 15–25 °C below Tj,max for production reliability.

swap_risks: CRITICAL CAPACITOR ESR OSCILLATION RISK: TLV1117-33IDCYR is stable with low-ESR ceramic MLCCs (>= 1 µF, p.26), whereas AMS1117-3.3 is NOT ceramic-cap stable (ESR window: See datasheet ESR curve). Using an ultra-low-ESR MLCC on AMS1117-3.3 can trigger control-loop oscillation.
CAUTION OUTPUT CAPACITANCE: Minimum Cout differs by 22x (AMS1117-3.3: 22 µF p.4 vs TLV1117-33IDCYR: 1 µF p.26); account for MLCC DC-bias derating.
HIGH LOAD CURRENT DERATING: TLV1117-33IDCYR supplies up to 800 mA (p.5) compared to AMS1117-3.3 at 1000 mA (p.1); confirm peak inrush and thermal dissipation margin.
CAUTION DROPOUT HEADROOM: Typical dropout differs (AMS1117-3.3: 1100 mV p.3 vs TLV1117-33IDCYR: 800 mV p.8); verify Vin,min - Vout >= Vdo across temperature and load corners.
engineering_verdict: AMS1117-3.3 (Advanced Monolithic Systems, SOT-223-3) and TLV1117-33IDCYR (Texas Instruments, SOT-223-3) are Level 2 Functional / Tuning Required alternatives: the PCB land pattern is compatible, but passive retuning or rating derating is mandatory because ceramic output capacitor ESR stability difference; minimum output capacitance requirement differs 22x; Iout,max rating drops >=20%. Under a representative 5 V → 3.3 V rail at 150 mA (255 mW), estimated self-heating is ΔTj ≈ 22.9 °C on AMS1117-3.3 (θJA 90 °C/W) vs 24.3 °C on TLV1117-33IDCYR (θJA 95.4 °C/W), while quiescent draw spans a 76.9x ratio (5000 µA (p.3) vs 65 µA (p.8)). Primary bench gotchas to watch: AMS1117-3.3 "NOT Ceramic-Cap Stable — Requires 22 uF Solid Tantalum (No Numeric ESR Window Published)" (p.4) and TLV1117-33IDCYR "CRITICAL Dual-Silicon Transition (New CMOS vs. Legacy Bipolar) Under Same OPN" (p.29). BOM decision: Choose AMS1117-3.3 when load current exceeds 800 mA (up to 1000 mA); choose TLV1117-33IDCYR when battery sleep budget demands 65 µA Iq or your BOM standardizes on low-ESR MLCC ceramic output capacitors. Always verify Pin 1 orientation (TOP_VIEW p.1 vs TOP_VIEW p.3) and official datasheets on hardware prototypes prior to production.
